label: About
title: About Where the Water Turns
short_blurb: A daily generated front page where the image is the interface.
body: Daily Frontpage is a daily generated interactive front page. Each edition starts from recent saved signals and source research, becomes a new image-led scene, and stays explorable in the archive. The image is the interface: visible marks, objects, and surfaces in the scene open the real sources that shaped the day.

This iteration began with 1212 recent saved-signal files and 949 captured links, then narrowed the page to 6 source windows around @palekirill: two works from my safe haven series, created last year for the verse x artist rooms... and @youwillmakemaps: I’m always thinking about Hiro Isono (b. 1945 - d. 2013) He understood, plus 4 more. A source image from pbs.twimg.com helped set the palette, contrast, edge behavior, and gesture. The scene became Where the Water Turns: An electric wetland architectural section, viewed in elevated three-quarter cutaway: one continuous cobalt-to-lavender channel threads three unequal grassy banks, the near shoreline exposing a shallow curved earth face. Scarred chalk birches crop through the upper edge; their reflections fracture sideways beneath them. After the image was made, a plate-reading pass mapped 6 visible regions and the mask audit tightened them against Broken pale birch reflections in the left-center water, Elongated dark-edged scar on the foremost birch, and Exposed angular rock face on the lower-left bank.

typography.rationale: Bricolage Grotesque and Space Grotesk fit record, arcade, and listening-room editions while Fraunces keeps source captions tactile.
